articleTitle: A magnetron using an NdFeB magnet
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: Summary form only given. One particular magnetron has been reduced to a quarter of its original weight by replacing the horseshoe-shaped Alnico magnets with a magnetic circuit which includes Neodymium Iron Boron (NdFeB) magnets. The basic steps taken in the redesign process and the most important aspects that needed to be considered when using NdFeB as a magnet for use in a magnetron design, are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Iron-neodymium-boron magnets produced by melt-spin processing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: The author discusses developments in chill-block melt spinning of FeNdB magnets and the continuing search for methods by which anisotropy can be introduced in the ribbon either during the melt spinning or by a single subsequent processing step.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The potential for Nd-Fe-B magnets in electrical machines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: Summary form only given. The author considers the design opportunities which Nd-Fe-B magnets offer in various classes and topologies of permanent magnet excited machine. This is done by taking a quick tour through the industrial drive, computer peripheral, consumer product, aerospace, and automotive market sectors and describing some specific applications. Some of the design considerations for the successful utilisation of Nd-Fe-B are highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field computation and permanent magnets
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: The calculation of electromagnetic fields is discussed with particular attention to the representation of hard magnetic materials. The material models extend from the simplest representation of very hard materials to more complex methods for materials to more complex methods for materials that are anisotropic and show a mixture of reversible and irreversible magnetisation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Magnetic, mechanical and environmental properties of NdFeB magnets-a user's view
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: Sintered NdFeB magnets show some promise in comparison with SmCo alloys particularly in terms of room temperature energy product and mechanical properties. Commercial availability is now such that they are worth considering for high performance machines. Therefore a programme of evaluation has begun to establish the properties of proprietary NdFeB magnets (and variability), and to some extent relate them to microstructure and composition, to aid design through a better understanding of magnet behaviour. Properties evaluated include: room and elevated temperature magnetic behaviour; resistivity; physical and mechanical properties; environmental stability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: The processing of Nd-Fe-B permanent magnet alloys by a number of different routes is discussed. The routes are: conventional powder route; Goldschmidt powder route; atomisation powder route; hydrogen decrepitation route; casting and hot working routes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: A range of materials was investigated including low and high coercivity magnets, bonded magnequench and cobalt containing alloys. The effect of temperature including irreversible and reversible changes of magnetization are discussed. Magnets with two different working points were investigated. Time effects were determined for magnets held at 100 degrees C for up to 200 hours. It was found that the higher coercivity H/sub cM/ the better is the temperature stability of the magnet. The highest coercivity materials are produced by using hydrogen decrepitation of the magnet powder.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The significance of magnet properties for applications in electromechanical devices
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: Summary form only given. The author deals with the general question: what (magnetic) properties must magnets have to make them optimally usable for applications in electromechanical devices such as motors, generators, actuators and simple levitation systems. Two kinds of magnets are considered, ferrites and rare earth magnets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on New Permanent Magnet Materials and their Applications
abstract: The author describes the powder processing technology used to produce the two major groups of permanent magnetic materials, these are the hard ferrite (SrFe/sub 12/O/sub 19/ or BaFe/sub 12/O/sub 19/) and rare earth (SmCo/sub 5/ based and NdFeB) permanent magnet groups. Some magnetic properties and uses are also briefly discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
